title: An army left like eaten straw
translation: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant? Did He not bring their plot to nothing? He sent against them flocks of birds, pelting them with stones of baked clay, and left them like straw eaten down.
body: Tradition names **Abraha’s Yemeni army**, in Muhammad’s birth year. Kropp: Abraha’s inscribed campaigns come **decades earlier**. Dye, after de Prémare, hears a midrash on **3 Maccabees’** elephants. Cuypers links “eaten straw” to Exodus 15:7. On divine might, **Luther’s Magnificat**: Mary’s word makes “all the strong feeble, all the mighty weak.”
question: Does Surah 105 remember a real campaign by Abraha, or retell an older legend of elephants and divine rescue?
source_label: Qur’an Seminar Commentary on Q 105 (Kropp, Dye, Cuypers) · Luther, Magnificat
